title: BRIDGING EXPLAINABILITY AND EMBEDDINGS: BEE AWARE OF SPURIOUSNESS

bias_targets.methodology: Extracting class-neutral concepts from datasets and ranking them based on their geometric similarity to learned class weights in a linear probe, then evaluating their impact through zero-shot prompting and generative counterfactual testing across vision and language datasets.
Analyzing classifier weights to detect gender as a learned spurious correlation when predicting the 'Blond Hair' attribute in the CelebA dataset, and measuring robustness via worst-group accuracy.

Identifying spurious correlations between toxicity classifications and mentions of racial or ethnic groups in the CivilComments dataset by tracking how fine-tuning perturbs pretrained representations.

Evaluating the model's reliance on religious identity terms as non-causal shortcuts for toxicity classification in the CivilComments dataset using the BEE (Bridging Explainability and Embeddings) framework.
